title: Mean, Median and Mode
seo_title: Sec 2 Mean, median and mode Worksheets: Free Secondary 2 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: mean, mode and median as measures of central tendency for a set of data; purposes and use of mean, mode and median
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 averages worksheets: find the mean, median, mode and range, work out a missing value from the mean, compare two data sets and choose the best average. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mean = total ÷ how many. Median = middle value in order. Mode = most common. Range = largest − smallest.
key_sub: Always put the data in order before finding the median.
body_html:
How it works

  • Mean: add up all the values and divide by how many there are.
  • Median: put the values in order and find the middle one (or halfway between the middle two).
  • Mode: the value that appears most often.
  • Range: largest − smallest. It shows how spread out the data is.
Example

Find the mean, median, mode and range of 5, 9, 2, 9, 10.

Mean: 35 ÷ 5 = 7.

In order: 2, 5, 9, 9, 10, so the median is 9.

Mode: 9. Range: 10 − 2 = 8.

Answer: 7, 9, 9 and 8

Example

The mean of 4 numbers is 6. Three are 3, 5 and 8. Find the fourth.

Total = 4 × 6 = 24.

24 − 16 = 8.

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

  • Finding the median without putting the values in order first.
  • Giving the position instead of the value: for 7 values the median is the 4th value, not 4.
  • Dividing by the wrong number when finding the mean.
  • Giving the largest value as the range instead of largest − smallest.

faq.q: What is the difference between mean, median and mode?
faq.a: The mean is the total shared equally, the median is the middle value in order, and the mode is the most common value.

faq.q: How do I find the median of an even number of values?
faq.a: Put them in order and find the two middle values. The median is halfway between them.
No. The range measures spread: largest minus smallest. A smaller range means more consistent data.
Use the mode for the most common item, the median when there are outliers, and the mean when you want to use every value.

items.q: Which average should you use for shoe sizes when ordering stock for a shop?
items.e: The shop wants the size sold most often: the mode. A mean such as 5.7 is not a real shoe size.

items.q: Salaries in a small firm are $20 000, $22 000, $23 000, $24 000 and $150 000. Which average best represents a typical salary?
items.e: The $150 000 is an outlier that pulls the mean up. The median ($23 000) is more typical.

items.q: What does the range tell you?
c: How spread out the data is
items.e: The range = largest − smallest. It measures how spread out the data is.

items.q: Which set of data has no mode?
items.e: In 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 every value appears once, so there is no mode.

c: The mean is one of the values
The mode is the middle value
The median of an odd number of values is one of the values
The range is bigger than the mean
items.e: With an odd number of values the median is the middle value itself, so it is one of the values.

items.q: Rachel's mean score in 4 games is 15. What must she score in the 5th game to raise her mean to 16?
items.e: She needs a total of 5 × 16 = 80. She has 60, so she needs 20.

items.q: Five numbers have a mean of 8. Which list could they be?

items.e: The middle two are 5 and 8, and halfway between is 6.5.

items.q: Team A's mean score is 12 with range 3. Team B's mean score is 12 with range 15. Which statement is correct?
c: Team A's scores are more consistent
The teams are the same in every way
items.e: The means are the same, but Team A has a smaller range, so Team A's scores are more consistent.

items.q: A data set is 7, 7, 8, 10, 13. If 13 is changed to 30, which average changes?
items.e: The median (8) and mode (7) stay the same. The total changes, so the mean changes.

items.q: The mean age of 3 children is 8. Their ages are all different whole numbers. What is the largest possible age of the oldest?
items.e: The total is 24. The other two must be at least 1 and 2, so the oldest can be 24 − 3 = 21.
